analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift files (SandboxSetupTests.swift, SandboxWorkDiskTests.swift). Every changed range adds a `waitlist: .approved` argument to SandboxSetupFlow initializers. The flow constructor evidently gained a waitlist dependency, so tests inject an approved state. The tests also assert that a stopped, waitlisted enrollment tells the user it keeps waiting and to rerun `darkbloom sandbox setup`, that setup never passes --force, and that unattended reruns apply only slot-adding plans.

No production code is in the supplied units, so I could not review how the waitlist gate is implemented or whether the default (non-test) path fails closed. The injected `.approved` stub exists only in test code. Related threat IDs: TB-013/T-061 (installer download and run as owner, with CoordinatorStub replacing the network in tests) and A-019. The tests use stubbed https://sandbox.invalid and a fake installer inside a CLICommandSandbox, so they do not touch real keychain, network or root settings, and no secrets appear.

The next pass should check the production SandboxSetupFlow, specifically that the waitlist parameter defaults to a real check that fails closed and that `.approved` is not reachable from release code. This evidence cannot settle that, so there are no findings.
